Ana, Connor — quick legal read and proposed approach.

Key principles we recommend:
1) Output ownership: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Content and Customer Output. Redwood shall have no rights to re-use Customer Output to train or improve models absent express, written opt-in on the Order Form."

2) Operational exceptions: "Notwithstanding the above, Redwood may use ephemeral, technical copies of Customer Output for debugging, caching (KV cache), and to comply with support requests, provided such uses are limited, logged, and not used to improve model weights."

3) Feedback license: "Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use feedback and telemetry solely to provide the Service and for aggregated, de-identified analytics; Redwood shall not use Customer Output or Customer Content to train models for external customers or productize verbatim Customer Output."

4) Order Form checkbox: We can accept a 'Training and feedback' checkbox with two options: (a) Opt-in: Redwood may use de-identified Customer Data and Feedback to improve models; (b) Opt-out: Redwood will exclude Customer Data from training pipelines for 36 months; parties may negotiate a price adjustment for opt-out. Also include a field for any additional scope (e.g., limited aggregate tuning).

I'll attach a proposed redline (Redwood_proposed_redline_MSA_20271120.docx) with snippet text. If Veridex needs Productization carveouts for internal-only use, we should try to define 'productization' narrowly.

If Veridex insists on ownership of model improvements derived from their data, that's a non-starter without a commercial carveout; we should escalate pricing/credits.

Laura Bennett

Ana — thanks and appreciate the candor. From a deal standpoint we want to keep momentum. Practical proposal:
- Redwood agrees to an explicit Order Form checkbox (default: opt-in). If Veridex chooses opt-out, we will provide a 15% per-token pricing credit on hosted usage for the contracted term.
- Opt-in: Redwood may use de-identified telemetry and aggregate signals to improve models; no direct productization of verbatim customer output.
- Opt-out: Veridex data excluded from training pipelines for 24 months; Redwood will still retain ephemeral telemetry for operational reliability (latency/availability) but will commit to process controls and deletion timelines.

If Legal (Laura) can sign off on the short Order Form clause, we can get procurement to greenlight quickly. Connor — do you have a preferred time for a quick alignment call?
